paragraphs.text: Create an isolated folder for every new DSH session and keep it synchronized with the session title.
# Session Folders
**One isolated folder per new conversation, with names that stay in sync with the session title.**
中文文档

Session Folders is a DSH host and client plugin for temporary or uncategorized conversations.
Every

new session in the default workspace gets its own working directory without creating
another sidebar
workspace or changing workspace ownership.
## Why

Scratch conversations often share the same default directory. One chat can leave scripts,
downloads,

or test files that confuse the next chat. Session Folders isolates those files
at the filesystem le
vel while preserving DSH's existing workspace and history model.
## Features

- Creates one folder for each new conversation in the default workspace.
- Uses the first message as

an initial readable name.
- Renames the folder when the generated or edited session title changes.

- Resolves collisions with `-2`, `-3`, and so on.
- Uses the native Windows folder picker for the pa

rent directory.
- Checks that the selected folder is accessible.
- Supports immediate creation or cr

eation on the first message.
- Recovers folders and title synchronization after a DSH restart.
- Kee

ps DSH's Open In button and local-file actions pointed at the active session folder.
- Never creates

extra workspace entries or changes historical workspace ownership.
- Leaves files written to explic
it absolute paths elsewhere untouched.
## Requirements

- DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0`
- Node.js 22 or newer for development

## Setup
Open **Plugins → Installed plugins → Session Folders**.
The configuration embedded in the plugin detail page provides:

- **Choose folder…** — select the parent directory used for new session folders.
- **Use default wor

kspace** — clear the custom parent directory.
- **Create on open** — allocate a folder as soon as a

new chat is opened.
- **Create on first message** — avoid empty folders by waiting for the first pro

chat is opened.
- **Create on first message** — avoid empty folders by waiting for the first prompt.

The selected folder is checked for accessibility. If a folder cannot be used, the session
continues
in the default workspace instead of blocking the conversation.
## Configuration
| Key | Default | Description |

| `enabled` | `true` | Enable per-session folders |
| `root` | `''` | Parent folder; empty uses the

default workspace |
| `creationMode` | `immediate` | `immediate` or `first-message` |
| `workspacePa

th` | `''` | Optional workspace override for advanced setups |
| `maxNameChars` | `60` | Maximum fol

onal workspace override for advanced setups |
| `maxNameChars` | `60` | Maximum folder-name length |
## Scope and behavior

Session Folders affects only new, top-level sessions whose original working directory is
the default

workspace. Historical sessions, subagent sessions, and sessions in other
workspaces are left unchan

kspace. Historical sessions, subagent sessions, and sessions in other
workspaces are left unchanged.

The session header keeps the original workspace path. Only the effective working directory
changes t

hrough `ctx.workingDirectory.set(agent, path)`, which is durable and replayed by DSH.
The client plu

gin mirrors that effective directory into DSH's session UI when the required
client interface is ava
ilable, so directory-opening controls target the managed folder.

Each managed folder contains `.dsh-per-session-folder.json`. This marker lets the plugin
recover its

folder after a restart. Folders created by the earlier development name retain
their legacy marker
and are adopted automatically.
## Limitations

- Only operations that resolve relative to the current working directory are isolated.
Absolute path

s intentionally written elsewhere are not intercepted or moved.
- Changing the parent directory affe

cts only future sessions. Existing folders stay put.
- The plugin never deletes or archives folders

automatically.
- Renaming a folder can invalidate an old path already mentioned earlier in a model t

urn.
The next model step receives a working-directory change notice.

usion, path failure fallback, deferred creation, and client directory syncing.
